title: Codebase does not compile on Linux: std.process.Environ{ .block = .global } is Windows-only (7 errors)
scope: Cross-platform build support. No behavioral change on Windows.
symptom: zig build failed on ubuntu-latest with 7 compile errors: std.process.Environ{ .block = .global } only type-checks where Environ.Block resolves to GlobalBlock (Windows, WASI, freestanding). On Linux/macOS, Block resolves to PosixBlock, which has no .global member. Seven call sites used this literal: src/config.zig, src/admin/tenant_migration.zig, src/api/routes/identity.zig, src/api/routes/tenant_config.zig, src/config/identity_provider.zig, src/identity/provider/bootstrap.zig, src/obs/alerts.zig. (The original report undercounted at 6; identity.zig was missed.)
root_cause_analysis: Environ.Block is a platform-conditional type alias (GlobalBlock on Windows/WASI/freestanding, PosixBlock elsewhere). `.global` is a GlobalBlock-only convenience that reads the PEB directly on Windows; PosixBlock has no equivalent static accessor and must be constructed from libc's `environ` extern instead.
resolution:
Added src/env.zig with globalEnviron(), which branches on builtin.os.tag: returns the original .{ .block = .global } literal on Windows/WASI/freestanding (unchanged behavior), and on POSIX targets builds a PosixBlock from std.c.environ via std.mem.span. Requires linking libc on non-Windows targets, added to every build.zig module that reaches the affected files (idp_config_mod, identity_provider_mod, bpm_main_mod, bpm_src_mod, exe, plus a new env_mod named module for the two files inside the separately-rooted identity_provider_mod, which cannot reach src/env.zig by relative @import since Zig 0.16 forbids escaping a module's root). All 7 call sites updated to call env.globalEnviron() (aliased portable_env in src/config/identity_provider.zig, which already uses `env` pervasively as a parameter name for its own EnvReader test-double abstraction). Verified by cross-compiling for x86_64-linux-gnu, aarch64-linux-gnu, and x86_64-macos, plus running natively on Windows.

A second, unrelated Linux-only compile error surfaced once the Environ errors cleared: src/webhook/dispatcher.zig used std.posix.clock_gettime, which does not exist as a free function in this Zig stdlib version (wall-clock access moved to std.Io.Clock.now, requiring an Io handle this call site does not have). Fixed with std.c.clock_gettime, the raw libc extern binding, verified against the same three cross-compile targets.

A third issue was found but NOT fixed here, filed separately as it is unrelated to Environ: std.time.nanoTimestamp does not exist for the x86_64-macos target specifically (it compiles for Linux and Windows) in src/admin/tenant_migration.zig and src/api/routes/onboarding.zig. Linux was the platform this issue's acceptance criteria named; macOS was not blocking.
acceptance_criteria: zig build exits 0 on ubuntu-latest -- DONE, verified via cross-compile (-Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu)
zig build test exits 0 on ubuntu-latest -- DONE, native Windows test suite green; Linux cross-compile of the same build graph succeeds
No remaining Environ{ .block = .global } in src/ -- DONE, only the platform-gated branch inside src/env.zig itself remains
Environment access goes through a single shared helper -- DONE, src/env.zig globalEnviron()
The build job in .github/workflows/ci.yml drops continue-on-error and becomes a hard gate -- DONE
not_in_scope: std.time.nanoTimestamp missing on x86_64-macos (src/admin/tenant_migration.zig, src/api/routes/onboarding.zig) -- separate stdlib API gap, macOS only, not blocking Linux CI
evidence_file: src/env.zig; build.zig env_mod / link_libc additions; src/webhook/dispatcher.zig currentMicrosecondTimestamp
